review_candidates.title: Manager, Climate Investment Facility
review_candidates.description: Location: Republic of Korea, HQ City: Seoul Contract Type: Staff Grade: G10 Salary scale: International Scale End date of appointment 36 months Deadline: 25/09/2026 Job Reference: New-RP26-66 Please note that the deadline is based on Korean Standard Time Zone (KST, UTC+9) INTRODUCTION TO GGGI The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page. The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is developing, in partnership with the European Commission, a proposal for the Global Gateway Climate Investment Facility. The proposed four-year, EUR 10 million Facility would provide flexible, demand-driven technical assistance to EU partner countries to accelerate implementation of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) by transforming climate commitments into investment-ready opportunities and financed implementation pathways. The proposed Facility would operate through an integrated Policy–Project–Finance model, supporting enabling policy and institutional frameworks, project preparation and investment structuring, and climate finance and investment mobilization. It is expected to support up to 15 partner countries and contribute to mobilizing at least EUR 1 billion in NDC- and Global Gateway-aligned investment, including at least EUR 750 million in private capital. This position is being prepared in anticipation of implementation of the proposed Facility. The proposal remains under development and no employment commitment arises from this Job Description. Recruitment and appointment to the position will be conditional on signature and entry into force of the Contribution Agreement between GGGI and the European Commission, confirmation of the approved project structure and budget, and completion of GGGI recruitment procedures. Position Summary The Manager will provide overall leadership, strategic direction, portfolio management and coordination for the proposed Facility. The Manager will lead development and implementation of a global pipeline of policy, project preparation and financing interventions; serve as the principal day-to-day interface with DG INTPA, EU Delegations, partner-country governments and the Facility Steering Committee; and ensure that approved interventions are delivered to high technical, fiduciary and results standards. The role will combine program leadership, investment origination, sustainable finance expertise, stakeholder management, resource allocation, quality assurance and donor reporting across a geographically and technically diverse portfolio. PURPOSE Lead the establishment and overall management of the Global Gateway Climate Investment Facility. Provide strategic leadership for a global, demand-driven portfolio of technical assistance interventions supporting NDC implementation, Global Gateway priorities, and the mobilization of public and private investment. Lead the identification, prioritization, design, and development of Facility interventions across the Policy–Project–Finance continuum, ensuring that support addresses material barriers to investment and implementation. Oversee the development of Project Information Notes (PINs) and maintain a high-quality pipeline of interventions and investment opportunities for consideration by the Facility Steering Committee. Drive the Facility’s contribution toward its proposed investment mobilization, project advancement, policy, institutional, and partnership targets, with particular attention to mobilizing private capital and creating opportunities for European participation. Ensure coherence across the Project Management Unit, Project Support Unit, Project Technical Unit, GGGI country and regional teams, global technical specialists, and external service providers involved in Facility delivery. Provide technical and managerial leadership on complex climate investment issues, including sustainable finance, project preparation, transaction structuring, adaptation finance, public investment management, blended finance, and carbon finance. ENGAGEMENT Serve as the principal GGGI counterpart for the European Commission on the Facility and maintain regular strategic and operational engagement with DG INTPA. Support the establishment and effective functioning of the Facility Steering Committee and present proposed interventions, portfolio updates, implementation progress, risks, and matters requiring strategic guidance or decision. Build and maintain strong working relationships with EU Delegations to identify country priorities, develop Facility pipelines, coordinate interventions, and ensure alignment with Global Gateway priorities and relevant EU initiatives. Engage senior government counterparts, including ministries of finance, planning authorities, sector ministries, regulators, national development banks, utilities, and other public institutions, to identify and advance high-impact opportunities for Facility support. Develop partnerships with European and international financial institutions, investors, companies, technology providers, engineering firms, advisory firms, development partners, and other relevant private-sector actors to advance investment opportunities and mobilize finance. Coordinate closely with GGGI regional and country teams, Sustainable Finance and other technical functions, and corporate support teams to mobilize expertise, maintain organizational alignment, and ensure effective implementation across the Facility portfolio. Represent the Facility in relevant external meetings, investment dialogues, technical forums, market-engagement activities, and other strategic platforms, communicating its objectives, pipeline, results, and opportunities for partnership. DELIVERY Leadpreparation and implementation of the Facility’s annual work plans, budgets, portfolio priorities, operational procedures, and resource-allocation decisions, subject to the governance arrangements established under the Contribution Agreement. Manage the end-to-end Facility pipeline, from country assessment and opportunity identification through technical scoping, PIN preparation, Steering Committee approval, implementation, monitoring, and completion. Ensure timely and high-quality delivery of approved interventions across policy and institutional reform, project preparation and investment structuring, climate finance, sustainable finance, carbon finance, and investment mobilization. Oversee allocation and deployment of Facility resources, including staff, consultants, framework agreements, technical service providers, and specialized expertise, ensuring value for money and compliance with GGGI and European Commission requirements. Establish and apply effective portfolio-management and quality-assurance processes to monitor implementation progress, budgets, risks, delivery milestones, technical quality, and achievement of expected results across multiple countries and interventions. Oversee monitoring, verification, and reporting of Facility results, including investment mobilization, project advancement, policy and institutional outcomes, stakeholder engagement, and other indicators established in the logical framework and Contribution Agreement. Ensure timely preparation of donor reports, Facility Steering Committee materials, management updates, and other required deliverables, while proactively identifying implementation risks, resolving delivery bottlenecks, and recommending corrective action. Requirements QUALIFICATIONS Master's degree in Economics, International Affairs, Public Policy, Environmental Management, or a related field. Preferably 10 years of professional experience in project management, sustainable finance, climate policy, carbon markets. At least 5 years of international work experience implementing and delivering projects in climate, green growth and/or sustainable finance, including substantive responsibility for project delivery across multiple countries or in collaboration with international partners and stakeholders. Demonstrated experience managing multiple multi-country, donor-funded projects, including budget, grant, and consultant management. Demonstrated experience designing new, complex programs of work, from origination to delivery. Fluency in both English is required; fluency in Franch and/or Spanish is a strong asset. Familiarity with GGGI mission, systems and processes is an advantage. FUNCTIONAL Strong project management and organizational skills to deliver complex, multi-country initiatives on time and within budget. Ability to translate technical and policy findings into clear guidance and knowledge products. Strong strategic foresight and ability to guide multiple programs of work towards mutually re-enforcing goals. Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills at all levels; excellent ability to maintain positive relationships with strategic resource and implementation partners. Demonstrated ability to work effectively across diverse country contexts and manage collaboration across cultures, institutions, and time zones. Flexibility and resilience to adapt to changing priorities, evolving donor and stakeholder needs, and uncertainty in project environments. Analytical and problem-solving skills with a focus on quality, efficiency, and innovation. CORPORATE Demonstrates GGGI's values of Integrity, Excellence, and Sustainability. Promotes a culture of transparency, inclusiveness, and collaboration. Fosters mutual respect, trust, and partnership in multicultural environments. Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

review_candidates.description: Amref Health Africa, founded in 1957, is the largest African-based international health development organisation. Headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, Amref implements programmes across 35 African countries , reaching more than 40 million people , with a strong operational presence in Africa and advocacy and fundraising offices in Europe and North America. Guided by its vision of lasting health change in Africa , Amref’s mission is to catalyse community-led, people-centred health systems and address the social determinants of health . Amref believes sustainable health transformation is driven from within communities and works to strengthen health systems while empowering communities to demand and access quality, affordable healthcare. JOB PURPOSE The HR Generalist supports the HR Business Partner, HQ in delivering reliable, responsive and employee-centred human resource services across the employee lifecycle. The role combines strong day-to-day people operations with future-focused HR practices by coordinating recruitment and onboarding, employee relations and experience, performance and talent processes, learning and future skills, workforce analytics, digital HR solutions and compliance. Through accurate service delivery, practical guidance, data-informed insights and continuous improvement, the role helps create an inclusive, agile and digitally enabled workplace while ensuring HR programmes and processes are implemented in line with organisational policies and applicable employment requirements. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES HR Operations, Employee Lifecycle and Service Delivery Coordinate employee lifecycle processes, including appointment, onboarding, probation and confirmation, contract changes and renewals, transfers, leave administration, separation and offboarding. Prepare accurate and timely employment documentation, employee correspondence and HR confirmations, and maintain trackers for contracts and other time-bound actions. Maintain complete, accurate and confidential employee records in the HR information system and personnel files, in line with data protection and records-management requirements. Support payroll and benefits administration by providing validated employee changes, completing routine reconciliations and resolving data discrepancies within agreed timelines. Provide first-line guidance to employees and managers on HR policies, processes and self-service tools, resolving routine queries and escalating complex or sensitive matters appropriately. Monitor recurring service queries and employee pain points and recommend practical improvements to the HR Business Partner. Talent Acquisition, Onboarding and Workforce Planning Support Support workforce planning by maintaining current headcount and vacancy information, tracking upcoming contract decisions and identifying emerging staffing or capability needs for review by the HR Business Partner. Coordinate recruitment processes from approved requisition through appointment, including job posting, application management, shortlisting administration, interview scheduling, candidate communication, pre-employment checks and appointment documentation. Support hiring managers to apply fair, inclusive and competency-based selection processes and maintain complete recruitment records in line with organisational policy. Coordinate onboarding and induction, including pre-boarding arrangements and scheduled follow-up, to help new employees integrate quickly and understand performance, culture, safeguarding and compliance expectations. Maintain recruitment and onboarding dashboards, monitor agreed timelines and candidate or new-joiner experience, and flag delays or improvement opportunities. Support development of talent pools for recurring and critical roles in line with approved workforce priorities. Employee Relations, Experience, Wellbeing and Culture Provide first-line support on routine employee relations matters, maintain accurate case records and refer complex, high-risk or sensitive cases to the HR Business Partner. Support fair and consistent implementation of employee relations processes, including attendance, conduct, grievance and performance-related matters, within established procedures. Coordinate employee listening, engagement, wellbeing and recognition initiatives; analyse feedback and track agreed actions with relevant leaders and teams. Gather feedback at key moments in the employee journey and use it to recommend improvements to employee experience and HR service delivery. Promote an inclusive, respectful and psychologically safe workplace by reinforcing organisational values, equity and inclusion, safeguarding expectations and relevant people policies. Performance, Talent, Learning and Future Skills Coordinate key stages of the performance management cycle, including goal setting, check-ins, review periods, documentation, completion tracking and follow-up with managers and employees. Support talent review, succession and employee development processes under the guidance of the HR Business Partner and relevant specialist teams. Coordinate learning-needs inputs and learning activities, including nominations, logistics, attendance, evaluation and maintenance of accurate training records. Track individual development plans, career-development actions and agreed learning commitments and provide completion and impact updates. Support initiatives that build future-relevant capabilities, including digital fluency, data literacy, collaboration, adaptability and people-management skills. People Analytics and Workforce Insights Maintain accurate workforce dashboards and trackers covering headcount, vacancies, contract status, recruitment, onboarding, turnover, absence, performance, learning and other agreed people indicators. Compile and analyse workforce data, identify patterns and emerging risks, and prepare concise reports and insights for the HR Business Partner and management decision-making. Support data quality checks, reconciliations and consistent use of workforce definitions across HR records, systems and reports. Translate employee and workforce data into practical follow-up actions and track whether agreed interventions deliver the intended improvement. HR Technology, Automation and Continuous Improvement Promote effective use of the HR information system, employee and manager self-service tools and approved digital workflows, and provide user guidance where required. Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise or automate repetitive HR processes while maintaining appropriate controls and a positive employee experience. Use approved digital and artificial intelligence-enabled tools responsibly to improve accuracy, insight and turnaround time, while ensuring data privacy, human oversight and compliance with organisational requirements. Maintain clear process maps, user guides and standard operating materials and support adoption of new HR tools and ways of working. Gather user feedback after process or technology changes and recommend refinements based on service data and employee experience. Policy, Risk, Governance and Change Support Support consistent application of organisational HR policies, procedures and internal controls and monitor completion of required documentation. Help ensure HR processes comply with applicable employment legislation, data protection, safeguarding and organisational requirements. Prepare documentation for internal and external audits, maintain agreed action trackers and support timely closure of HR findings and risks. Support people-related change initiatives through accurate employee data, coordinated communications, stakeholder follow-up and practical adoption support. Contribute operational insights to policy and process reviews and help communicate approved changes in clear and accessible language. Handle employee information with discretion and maintain strict confidentiality in all HR activities. Qualifications Academic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration or a related field. Professional Qualifications / Memberships Higher Diploma in Human Resource Management, CHRP qualification or an equivalent professional credential. Current membership of the Institute of Human Resource Management or another relevant professional body, as applicable. Experience Minimum of three (3) to five (5) years of relevant experience in an HR generalist or comparable role. Demonstrated experience supporting HR operations, recruitment and onboarding, employee relations, performance and learning processes, HR reporting and compliance in a diverse work environment. Practical experience using an HR information system and workforce data to support service delivery and decision-making. Exposure to HR digitalisation, process improvement, employee-experience or organisational-change initiatives is an advantage. Knowledge, Skills and Competencies Sound knowledge of end-to-end HR operations, employee lifecycle processes and contemporary people practices. Working knowledge of Kenyan employment legislation, HR compliance, governance, data protection and safeguarding requirements. Ability to provide responsive, accurate and practical HR support while maintaining a strong employee and manager service orientation. Strong employee-relations judgement, including the ability to recognise risk, maintain accurate records and escalate matters appropriately. Strong planning, project-coordination and organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver within agreed timelines. Strong interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships across teams and levels. Analytical capability, including the ability to interpret workforce data, identify trends and present clear, decision-relevant insights. Digital literacy and proficiency in HR information systems, Microsoft Office applications, reporting tools and employee self-service platforms. Curiosity and confidence to learn and responsibly apply emerging HR technologies, automation and artificial intelligence-enabled tools. Process-improvement mindset, with the ability to identify inefficiencies, propose practical solutions and support adoption of new ways of working. Adaptability and change orientation, with an interest in future workforce capabilities and evolving employee expectations. Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with professionalism, discretion and integrity. Commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, safeguarding, wellbeing and a positive employee experience. Collaborative, accountable and service-oriented approach, with a commitment to continuous learning and high-quality delivery. Additional Information Please submit your CV or resume highlighting relevant skills and experience along with a cover letter detailing why you are the best fit for this position. Amref Health Africa is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff to share this commitment.
